GameAnalytics MCP Server: Chat with your game data from Claude, Cursor, Codex, and more
Anton Liakhovich
Last updated: Nov 03, 2026
min read
GameAnalytics introduces its own Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, a hosted way to connect your game data directly to AI assistants. Available as a standalone subscription at $149 per month or included with PipelineIQ Pro.
What if your game data could answer you directly? For years, game teams have relied on dashboards, SQL queries, and scattered tools to understand what their players are doing. Useful? Absolutely. Fast and intuitive? Not always. As AI reshapes how developers work, we asked ourselves a simple question: what if your game data could just talk back?
Today,
the GameAnalytics MCP Server
is the answer. It’s a hosted bridge between your GameAnalytics data and AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Codex, and any other tool that supports the MCP standard. You add one URL (
https://mcp.gameanalytics.com
) to your AI tool, sign in with your GameAnalytics account through a standard OAuth flow, and start asking questions in plain language.
What the MCP server does
MCP is a standard that lets AI tools talk to external APIs in a structured way. The GameAnalytics MCP Server acts as the translator between your AI assistant and the GameAnalytics Metrics API. Instead of manually filtering dates and dimensions, you can open your preferred AI client and ask something like:
“Show me D7 retention for our iOS build last week, and compare it to the Android build.”
The server translates your request into the right API calls, pulls the data, and returns a summary your AI can reason about. Access is read-only. The server can see every Organization, Studio, and Game your account has access to, but it cannot change your data or settings.
Secure sign-in through OAuth
The first time you connect, your AI tool opens a sign-in page in your browser. You sign in with your GameAnalytics account, review a consent screen that names the AI tool asking for access, and choose Allow. From then on, the connection is live. You can revoke it any time by removing the server in your AI tool.
This is a significant change from how most game data integrations work today. There are no API keys to copy, no credentials to manage, and no custom auth setup. Standard OAuth, same pattern as signing in with Google.
Available two ways
The MCP Server is available two ways. Teams who want their game data inside their AI tools without the full data pipeline can get MCP Access on its own at $149 per month. PipelineIQ Pro includes MCP access alongside the Data Warehouse, Data Export, Metrics API, Organization API, and custom event fields.
What studios are doing with it
The MCP Server has already landed in production workflows across very different studios, and the ways teams are using it tell the story better than any example we could invent.
Blitz of Battle
is using the server to go beyond standard reporting. The publishing team is exploring correlations between metrics that would be too tedious to surface manually, which opens up a layer of analysis that most reporting workflows skip entirely.
GameAnalytics MCP Server worked better than expected. I was able to get further analyses done by looking at correlations of metrics that I wouldn’t normally be looking at. - Publishing Director, Blitz of Battle
Pitch Labs
is building autonomous agent pipelines around their product analytics. For teams building AI-native workflows, MCP has become infrastructure rather than a feature, and the Pitch Labs team moved on it the moment it launched.
MCP access is crucial in building any autonomous agent pipeline, especially for product analytics. The moment GameAnalytics launched the MCP server, we immediately upgraded our pipeline. - Derrick Ko, CEO and Co-Founder, Pitch Labs
Zero One
plugs the server into an entire agent chain that runs inside Cursor. The chain handles everything from ideation to monetization, with the GameAnalytics MCP Server as the plug-and-play data layer that validates whether each release actually moved the needle.
